node.label: Doug Owram
node.date_label: Promise of Eden (1980) · The Government Generation (1985) · Born at the Right Time (1996)
node.description: A Canadian intellectual and social historian whose work connects ideas about western expansion, the state and postwar generational change. His baby-boom synthesis treats childhood, consumer power and youth politics together; the reader used here disputes how representative its radical youth are.

proposed_edges.relationship: Relates the baby boom to child-centred households, consumer markets and psychological ideas about childhood.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Daniel Stoffman describes these arguments in his substantive review; this is named-reader mediation, not a reading of the whole book. He questions how distinctive the cohort itself was.

proposed_edges.relationship: Interprets Canadian youth politics through the scale and shared culture of the baby-boom generation.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Stoffman reports the interpretation but disputes the space given to radicals and the claim of broad generational sympathy. The qualification is part of this contribution record.
